title: One validator module per result: the door chunk stops growing with every RPC
shared_surfaces: packages/contract (the shared TS contract: RESULT_VALIDATORS becomes RESULT_LOADERS, parseRpcResult becomes async)
apps/console data layer (console-data-layer context): Door.parseRpcResult returns Result | Promise<Result>; rpc.ts:78-79 already awaits the door, so no call-site change
acceptance: generate() over the committed schema -> src/generated/results/ holds exactly one module per distinct method result def (43 today) plus validators.js holding only ServerFrame + ErrorEnvelope; running it twice is byte-identical
results/RunsPage.js source -> contains no ClipCandidate / ReviewSession / ReconcileReport validator code (grep of their $defs ids is empty)

await parseRpcResult('runs.page', {result:{items:[]}}) -> {ok:true, value:{items:[]}}, and the module registry shows only results/RunsPage.js was loaded (vi spy on the loader map: 1 call, key 'runs.page')
await parseRpcResult('preflight.run', {result:[{...report, state:'purple'}]}) -> invalid with path '/result/0/state' (every existing door.test case keeps passing, awaited)
a loader that rejects (chunk fetch failure) -> parseRpcResult resolves {ok:false, error:{kind:'unavailable_validator'...}} or the existing 'internal' mapping in contractDoor; it never throws
pnpm -C packages/contract check after deleting one generated results/*.js, or adding a stray one -> exit 1 naming the file (the gate diffs the whole generated tree, not a fixed list)

vite build + check-bundle -> 'door' (first-load: ServerFrame + ErrorEnvelope + door) <= 160,000 B js (today budget 516,000, measured 513,501); every 'door.result' chunk <= its own budget line; an unbudgeted validator chunk fails the gate
premise: packages/contract/scripts/codegen.mjs:68-98 - validatorFiles() compiles ServerFrame, ErrorEnvelope and every method's result def into ONE standalone module (standaloneCode(ajv, exported))

packages/contract/scripts/codegen.mjs:126-129 - meta.ts imports validators.js statically (`import * as v`) and builds RESULT_VALIDATORS from it, so any importer of the door pulls every method's validator

apps/console/src/app/compose.ts:15-16 - the console loads contractDoor as one lazy chunk 'in parallel with the first paint'; apps/console/src/data/socket.ts:94-97 drops /events frames until it resolves

apps/console/budgets/bundle.json:2 - the budget log records door 280,000 -> 516,000 B over seven features (tournament.results +52,443 B, clips +~80 KB, sandbox, review +~40 KB, prep +~28 KB) and states 'splitting the validators per method is codegen work in packages/contract'

apps/console/src/data/rpc.ts:78-79 - `const door = await opts.door; return door.parseRpcResult(method, text);` already sits in an async function, so an async per-method validator costs no call-site change

apps/console/scripts/check-bundle.mjs:28-30,70-74 - every dynamic chunk must match a named route or the gate fails, so per-result chunks need an explicit route rule (the budget stays a gate, not advisory)

packages/contract/scripts/check.mjs:31 + .ai/registry-map.json ipc-contract verdict - the drift gate diffs the fixed GENERATED_FILES list (recorded deviation); a dynamic file set forces the tree-wide diff, closing that deviation as a side effect
rollback: Three commits (codegen+generated tree; door/contract API; console door + budget). Revert in reverse order; the monolithic validators.js is regenerated by the reverted codegen.mjs with `pnpm -C packages/contract generate --no-export`, and bundle.json returns to the 516,000 line.
test_command: pnpm -C packages/contract test && pnpm -C packages/contract typecheck && pnpm -C packages/contract lint && pnpm -C packages/contract check && pnpm -C apps/console typecheck && pnpm -C apps/console test && pnpm -C apps/console build && node apps/console/scripts/check-bundle.mjs
runner_up: Outbound params door: generate params validators so encodeRpcRequest refuses an `as`-cast or stale param shape before the wire instead of an invalid_params round trip.
body:
## Summary
The contract compiles every RPC result validator into one 903 KB module that the console must load before it can read a single reply or /events frame. Split codegen output into one module per result def behind a lazy loader map, keep only ServerFrame + ErrorEnvelope eager, and make the per-chunk budget a gate.

## Description
Today `validatorFiles()` emits one standalone ajv module and `meta.ts` imports it statically, so the door chunk is the sum of every method ever added: the console's own budget log walks it from 280,000 to 516,000 B across seven features and names this exact split as owed codegen work. Measured offline with the same ajv settings: standalone ServerFrame is 194,190 chars of 902,558 (21%); the median per-result module is 11,788; the largest (ReviewSession) 274,653. So first paint + the live socket need about a fifth of today's door, and a page pays only for the methods it calls. This leans on codegen `generated-file-hygiene` (deterministic, banner-stamped, byte-identical output) and `drift-gating` / ipc-contract `drift-gates` (the gate must see new and deleted artifacts - a dynamic file set makes the curated-list deviation at check.mjs:31 impossible to keep). The public door API stays one door (ipc-contract `call-wrapping`): parseRpcResult becomes async and resolves the method's loader; parseEvent stays synchronous on the eager ServerFrame module, so the socket path is unchanged.

## Flow
- codegen: for each distinct result def, `standaloneCode(ajv, {validate: ref})` into `generated/results/<Def>.js` + `.d.ts`; validators.js keeps ServerFrame + ErrorEnvelope only.
- meta.ts: `RESULT_LOADERS: {[M in RpcMethod]: () => Promise<ValidateFn<RpcResult<M>>>}` as `() => import('./results/<Def>.js').then(m => m.validate)`.
- door.ts: `parseRpcResult` awaits the loader (memoized), maps a rejected import to a DoorError, never throws.
- check.mjs: diff the whole generated tree (missing, extra, changed).
- console: Door.parseRpcResult typed `Result | Promise<Result>`; check-bundle routes `node_modules/@shadowrunr/contract/src/generated/results/*` chunks to `door.result` with a per-chunk max; bundle.json door line drops to the measured first-load figure.

## Expected impact
The door the console waits on before its first /events frame shrinks by roughly 4/5 (projected <= 160,000 B from 513,501 B; ratio from the unminified measurement); each new RPC adds a chunk only its caller loads instead of raising everyone's first load; the drift gate covers the full generated tree.

## Evaluation
Claim: the first-load door chunk falls from 513,501 B to <= 160,000 B with no contract behaviour change.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no per-result modules, sync RESULT_VALIDATORS, fixed-list gate, door budget 516,000).
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first; check-bundle measures the built manifest deterministically
Result: better
Gate: architecture (contract API shape: parseRpcResult async; RESULT_VALIDATORS -> RESULT_LOADERS). Note: regenerated files are machine output and excluded from the ~800-line hand-written estimate (~350 hand lines).
evidence: wc -c validators.js -> 903110; grep -c '^function validate' -> 196. Offline split probe (same Ajv2020 options as codegen.mjs:69-75): monolith 902558; ReviewSession 274653, ServerFrame 194190, RunTranscriptResult 177338, ReconcileReport 128185, ClipCandidate 125354; median RankTableInfo 11788; smallest SimStartResult 1354. meta.ts:5 `import * as v from "./validators.js";`. bundle.json:2 '...door 280,000 -> 320,000 ... splitting the validators per method is codegen work in packages/contract ... Screens contract, measured: door 510,000 -> 516,000 (513,501 B'. rpc.ts:78 `const door = await opts.door;`.

critic.reason: High-value, measured codegen split with a real gate; sequence against B and the types-crate regen.

title: Tagged unions validate by their tag: a bad event names its real field
shared_surfaces: packages/contract (generated validators gain ajv `discriminator` dispatch; schema file and types.ts unchanged; validators.d.ts gains validateEventFrame / validateStreamEvent exports)
acceptance: parseEvent({type:'stream_end', ts_ms:5}) -> invalid, issues[0].message names 'reason' (today: path '' "must have required property 'seq'", the real violation is error 17 of 20 and dropped by MAX_ISSUES=10)

parseEvent({seq:9, run_id:'r', event:{type:'health', ts_ms:1}}) -> invalid, path '/event', issues[0].message names 'state', issues.length <= 2 (today: first issue "/event must have required property 'stream_id'", 36 errors)
parseEvent({...validStreamStart, audience_size:'three'}) -> invalid, path '/audience_size' (today: '' must have required property 'seq')
parseEvent({type:'teleport', ts_ms:1}) -> invalid, path '/type', message says the tag value is not in the union

parseRpcResult('run.transcript', {result:[validStreamStart, {type:'say', ts_ms:1, speaker:'lord'}]}) -> path '/result/1', message names 'text' (today: "/result/1 must have required property 'stream_id'")

codegen.test: the prepared validator schema carries a discriminator on exactly CalibrationOrigin(kind), Command(cmd), EngineError(kind), Op(op), StreamEvent(type), VoiceFrame(type), derived from the schema (every alternative requires the same const-valued property), never from a hand list
every line of the stored fixture transcript still passes parseEvent, and `pnpm -C packages/contract check` stays green (deterministic output)
premise: packages/contract/scripts/codegen.mjs:69-75 - Ajv2020 is built without the `discriminator` option, and the schema passed to it is the raw export (forTs only feeds json-schema-to-typescript)

packages/contract/schema/contract.schema.json $defs.StreamEvent - a 16-alternative oneOf, each alternative requiring a `type` property with a const; five more unions (CalibrationOrigin, Command, EngineError, Op, VoiceFrame) share the shape (schema scan: every alt requires one common const property)
packages/contract/schema/contract.schema.json $defs.ServerFrame - anyOf [EventFrame, ErrorEnvelope, StreamEvent], so a bare event is also tried as an envelope and an error frame first
packages/contract/src/door.ts:37 - MAX_ISSUES = 10; door.ts:53-57 - the DoorError's path/message is issues[0], i.e. whatever ajv happened to report first
packages/contract/src/door.ts:121-125 - parseEvent runs validateServerFrame on the whole frame; no routing by shape before validation

apps/console/src/data/contractDoor.ts:28-29 - an 'invalid' DoorError becomes the console's internal error carrying e.message and e.path, so the misleading path is what an operator and a bug report see
packages/contract/src/door.test.ts:118-122 - the only negative event test asserts kind 'invalid', never the path, which is why the wrong path has survived
rollback: Two commits (codegen discriminator + regenerated validators; door ServerFrame routing + tests). Reverting both and running `pnpm -C packages/contract generate --no-export` restores the current output byte-for-byte.
test_command: pnpm -C packages/contract test && pnpm -C packages/contract typecheck && pnpm -C packages/contract lint && pnpm -C packages/contract check && pnpm -C apps/console test
runner_up: Generated contract fixtures: the Rust side emits one serialized sample per result def and the contract suite validates each, turning 'generated type promises what the wire cannot carry' into a per-method test instead of one transcript fixture.
body:
## Summary
The door is the one place a wire mismatch is diagnosed at runtime, and for every tagged union it reports the wrong field. Validate tagged unions by their tag and route ServerFrame by shape, so the first issue is the real one.

## Description
ajv validates a plain oneOf by trying every alternative and reporting all their failures; the door then takes the first of at most ten. For StreamEvent (16 variants) that first issue is almost always about a variant the payload never claimed to be: a bare `stream_end` missing `reason` reports "must have required property 'seq'" (from the EventFrame branch of ServerFrame's anyOf), and the true violation is error 17 of 20, cut by MAX_ISSUES. A malformed `say` inside run.transcript reports a missing `stream_id`. This is ipc-contract `error-shape-mapping` (a handler may branch on and display only what the error truthfully says) and `generated-type-contracts` (the validator must describe the wire's own discrimination, which serde's internally-tagged enums already declare via a required const tag). Codegen derives the tagged set from the schema - every alternative requires one common const property - and adds `discriminator: {propertyName}` to a validator-only copy (the committed schema stays the Rust export), with Ajv's `discriminator: true`. door.ts stops validating ServerFrame as an anyOf: `error` -> ErrorEnvelope, `seq` -> EventFrame, else StreamEvent, each exported from the same module. Side effect: one branch is validated per event instead of up to 18.

## Flow
- codegen: `forAjv(schema)` walks $defs, tags qualifying oneOfs, exports validateEventFrame and validateStreamEvent alongside ServerFrame.
- door.ts: shape-route the frame, then validate with the one matching validator; EventMessage output unchanged.
- tests: path/message assertions for the five probes above; fixture transcript sweep unchanged.

## Expected impact
Every runtime contract violation on /events and in event-bearing results (run.transcript, review.session) names the field and the variant that actually failed, so drift found in the console points at the Rust type to fix instead of at a phantom 'seq'. The schema, TS types and accepted set do not change.

## Evaluation
Claim: for tagged-union payloads the door's first issue is the real violation.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass as written (probed against the committed validators: stream_end -> "'' must have required property 'seq'" with the real issue at index 16 of 20; enveloped health -> 36 errors, first names 'stream_id'; run.transcript bad say -> 17 errors, first names 'stream_id', real one at index 6).
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first
Result: better
Gate: contract (generated validator output changes; accepted payload set unchanged, proven by the fixture sweep and `check`).
evidence: node probe against src/generated/validators.js: validateServerFrame({type:'stream_end',ts_ms:5,reason:42}) -> 20 errors, first: '' "must have required property 'seq'"; enveloped {seq:9,run_id:'r',event:{type:'health',ts_ms:1}} -> 36 errors, first '/event' "must have required property 'stream_id'", the 'state' error at index 14; validateRunTranscriptResult([start,{type:'say',ts_ms:1,speaker:'lord'}]) -> 17 errors, first "/1 must have required property 'stream_id'", 'text' at index 6. Schema scan of oneOf defs whose alternatives all require one const property: CalibrationOrigin{kind}, Command{cmd}, EngineError{kind}, Op{op}, StreamEvent{type} (16 alts), VoiceFrame{type}. grep -n discriminator packages/contract/scripts packages/contract/src/generated/validators.js -> no matches.

critic.reason: Precisely evidenced, fully falsifiable; sequence with contract A.
